_comments: Contracts -> Contract Template Modifications: PRIMARY, so Modifications is its own rail item.
There was no row here at all, on the reasoning that the editor panel claims the related entity
so no chrome was needed. Wrong for the same reason as ParentContractID below: claiming the
relationship suppresses the stock GRID; it does not create a rail GROUP. Omitting the row left
it Auto, and the panel folded into Details.
DisplayName is the rail label. 'Modifications' rather than the entity's full name, which would
read 'Contract Template Modifications' in a rail on a Contract form — three words of context
the reader already has.
FORM CHROME — how OTHER apps' forms present the relationships our FKs create (plan §6.4/§7 item 11).
Contracts owns these rows because contracts created the FKs. This file is why the 'customer view'
(item 11) is mostly metadata rather than a screen: an organisation's agreements appear on Common's
Organization form, where someone looking at a customer already is.
Same file split as orders: collection declarations live in .entity-relationships.json, presentation
lives here. Both push to MJ: Entity Relationships; keeping them apart means a chrome tweak never
risks a collection blob.
Organization -> Contracts is PRIMARY and renamed 'Agreements' — the word the business uses, and
the word the plan's reviewers used throughout. 'Contracts' would also collide conceptually with
the app name in a sidebar that already says Contracts.
Person -> Contracts via PrimaryContactPersonID is 'More', not Primary. A person is the CONTACT on
an agreement, not its counterparty — the counterparty is always the organisation (ERD §4.1). Real
but secondary, which is exactly what More means.
Company -> Contracts: hidden. CompanyID says which of OUR legal entities is party to the
agreement, and it points at MJ CORE's Company (MJ: Companies) — not accounting's. Worth stating,
because the ERD calls it a cross-app reference and the @lookup key silently matches nothing if
you assume MJ_BizApps_Accounting: Companies (verified against __mj.EntityRelationship, 2026-08-18).
agreement — plumbing for multi-company reporting, not something a person opens a Company record
to browse. Every contract points at one, so the list is unbounded and useless as a related grid.
Entity -> Contracts: hidden. This is the polymorphic half of the creating pair (CreatingEntityID
is a real FK to __mj.Entity). Nobody opens the metadata row for 'Deals' to see every contract a
deal ever created — the useful direction is the other one, which IX_Contract_CreatingRecord serves.
Left visible it would put a contracts grid on an MJ CORE form, which is somebody else's screen.
Contract Template Provisions -> Modifications: hidden. 'Which contracts negotiated THIS clause'
is a genuinely interesting question — and it is a report, not a grid of join rows on the provision
form. Item 7's registry shows provisions; the analysis belongs on a purpose-built surface.
Contract -> Modifications is deliberately absent from this file: the modifications editor panel
CLAIMS that related entity (plan §6.4), which hides the stock grid without any metadata.
Contracts -> Contracts via SupersededByContractID: PRIMARY. This grid lists the contracts THIS
agreement supersedes.
REVERSED by Marcelo, 2026-08-21. This row previously set inclusion 'None' and hid the grid, on the
reasoning quoted here verbatim so the trade is not lost: the section would be 'a related list headed
something like Contracts that means contracts naming me as their successor... the useful direction is
what replaced this?, which is the FK on the record itself', and 'None rather than More: a grid whose
meaning has to be explained is worse than no grid.'
That argument was sound about the LABEL and wrong about the NEED. Seeing everything one agreement
replaces is a stated requirement (a contract may supersede several), and un-superseding one has to
happen somewhere. The objection is answered by naming it: DisplayName 'Supersedes' says which
direction it reads, so nothing has to be explained.
WHAT THIS GRID CAN AND CANNOT DO. It owns SEE and REMOVE - every superseded contract, openable, and
clearing a row's successor un-supersedes it. It cannot ADD: a related grid's New creates a brand-new
record, not a pointer to an existing one. That is why the Re-papering field panel still owns the
picker. Two surfaces, one each for the two halves.
Both flags are set because they are different layers (guide §7d): DisplayInForm is L0 - whether the
relationship is a candidate at all - and Configuration.UI.inclusion is L1 - whether it is first-class
on the rail. Primary without DisplayInForm renders nothing.
Contracts -> Contracts via ParentContractID: PRIMARY, and this was WRONG before.
I had it as 'None' reasoning that the lineage panel claims the relationship so the stock grid
should be suppressed. But 'None' means the ranker never sees it AT ALL — so the panel claiming
it got no chrome group, and under Layout:'left-nav' a contribution with no group folds into
Details. That is why the form had exactly one section.
Primary is what makes Lineage its own rail item. The panel still replaces the stock grid,
because that is what `relatedEntity` on the registration does — suppressing the grid and
having a rail entry are different mechanisms, and I had conflated them.
Contract Templates -> Provisions: PRIMARY. The provisions ARE the template's content.
Rail order on the template form is Details, then Provisions (ruled 2026-08-19). That falls out
of MJ's fixed band order — lead contributions → Details → Primary related → More — once the
Documents panel stops being a lead contribution on this entity. See the chromeGroup:'more' note
in record-files.panel.ts for why that is the only way to order Details ahead of it.
